# Overview

Beyond its causal-inference and survey-statistics surfaces, rmorie
includes signal-processing functions: periodogram, multitaper and
Welch spectral estimates, the short-time Fourier transform, the
Hilbert envelope, cepstra and cepstral pitch estimation. They apply to
audio and biomedical signals and to any regularly sampled series, such
as daily incident counts.

# A synthetic two-tone signal

```{r setup}
library(rmorie)

set.seed(42)
fs <- 1000                           # sampling rate (Hz)
t  <- seq(0, 1, by = 1 / fs)
sig <- sin(2 * pi * 50 * t) +
       0.5 * sin(2 * pi * 120 * t) +
       0.3 * rnorm(length(t))
```

# Basic FFT

```{r fft}
spec <- stats::fft(sig)
n    <- length(sig)
freq <- (0:(n / 2 - 1)) * fs / n
mag  <- Mod(spec)[1:(n / 2)]
peak_freqs <- freq[order(mag, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]]
peak_freqs
```

The largest peaks sit next to 50 Hz and 120 Hz, the two components of
the synthetic signal.

# Spectral density estimates

`morie_dsp_psd_periodogram()` returns the raw periodogram,
`morie_psdmt()` a multitaper estimate (`nw = 4` by default), and
`welch()` Welch's averaged-segment estimate. Each returns the
frequencies and the power spectral density:

```{r psd}
per <- morie_dsp_psd_periodogram(sig, fs = fs)
mt  <- morie_psdmt(sig, fs = fs)
wl  <- welch(sig, fs = fs, nperseg = 256L)

# frequency of the largest PSD value in each band (Hz)
peaks <- function(f, p) c(
  low  = f[f > 25 & f < 85][which.max(p[f > 25 & f < 85])],
  high = f[f > 95 & f < 145][which.max(p[f > 95 & f < 145])]
)
rbind(periodogram = peaks(per$freqs, per$psd),
      multitaper  = peaks(mt$frequencies, mt$psd),
      welch       = peaks(wl$extra$freqs, wl$filtered))
mt$n_tapers
```

All three put a peak next to 50 Hz and next to 120 Hz. Welch's
estimate trades frequency resolution (here `fs / nperseg`, about
3.9 Hz) for lower variance, so its peaks fall on the nearest bins of
that coarser grid. The Welch PSD values are in the `filtered` element
and its frequencies in `extra$freqs`.

# Short-time Fourier transform

`morie_rangayyan_stft()` returns the spectrogram matrix `Sxx`
(frequencies by time segments):

```{r stft}
st <- morie_rangayyan_stft(sig, fs = fs, nperseg = 128L)
dim(st$Sxx)
range(st$times)
```

# Envelope and cepstral pitch

`morie_dsp_hilbert_envelope()` returns the amplitude envelope of a
signal. `morie_cepstrum_pitch()` estimates a fundamental frequency
from the real cepstrum; on a harmonic signal at 150 Hz:

```{r cepstrum}
env <- morie_dsp_hilbert_envelope(sig)
length(env)

fs2 <- 8000
tt  <- seq(0, 0.5, by = 1 / fs2)
voiced <- rowSums(sapply(1:10, function(k) sin(2 * pi * k * 150 * tt) / k))
morie_cepstrum_pitch(voiced, fs = fs2)$f0
```

# Where to go next

- `morie_dsp_complex_cepstrum()` and `morie_dsp_homomorphic()` cover
  cepstral and homomorphic processing.
- `Spectrogram()`, `IStft()` and `reassigned_spectrogram()` are
  further time-frequency tools; see their help pages.
